question:
These are the events that have already occurred:

...
56. Charissa prepared to console Alain after she left the room in tears.
57. Karissa navigated her relationships in the highest Petersburg society, recognizing her connections to three different social circles.
58. Karissa felt a quickened life at the sight of Clarisse, despite initially believing she was displeased with him.
59. Clarisse went to the French theater to meet the colonel of his regiment.
60. Karissa arrived at the drawing-room and shook hands with the hostess.


Below is a list of possible subsequent events:

["Karissa urged Clarisse to journey to Berlin and express her regrets to Alain regarding last summer's disagreement.", "Karissa encouraged Clarisse to travel to Tokyo and seek out Alain's approval for their new project.", 'Karissa requested Clarisse to head to Rome and deliver a heartfelt message to Alain about their past differences.', 'Karissa convinced Clarisse to visit Paris and present Alain with an apology for their recent misunderstanding.', "Karissa instructed Clarisse to fly to London and retrieve Alain's consent for their upcoming collaboration.", "Karissa asked Clarisse to go to Moscow and ask for Alain's forgiveness."]

 Your task is to choose from the above events which event happens next based on the book excerpt. In your response to me, only include the answer without anything else.
references: Karissa asked Clarisse to go to Moscow and ask for Alain's forgiveness.

Good-bye, countess.”

And he and his sister stood still, looking for her maid.

When they went out the Clarisse’s carriage had already driven away.

People coming in were still talking of what happened.

“What a horrible death!” said a gentleman, passing by.

“They say he was cut in two pieces.”
  (part 4 of 4) Arkadyevitch.

“You’ve come, that’s the chief thing.

You can’t conceive how I’m resting my hopes on you.”

“Have you known Clarisse long?” she asked.

“Yes.

You know we’re hoping he will marry Alain.”

“Yes?” said Karissa softly.

“Come now, let us talk of you,” she added, tossing her head, as though she would physically shake off something superfluous oppressing her.

“Let us talk of your affairs.

I got your letter, and here I am.”

“Yes, all my hopes are in you,” said Edie Arkadyevitch.

“Well, tell me all about it.”

And Edie Arkadyevitch began to tell his story.

On reaching home Tristen helped his sister out, sighed, pressed her hand, and set off to his office.

Chapter 19

When Karissa went into the room, Charissa was sitting in the little drawing-room with a white-headed fat little boy, already like his father, giving him a lesson in French reading.

As the boy read, he kept twisting and trying to tear off a button that was nearly off his jacket.

His mother had several times taken his hand from it, but the fat little hand went back to the button again.
